title: Manipulating Attributes with jQuery
summary: Introduces .attr() for reading and writing HTML attributes such as img src and a href, noting that the class attribute can be read the same way.

concepts.heading: .attr() as getter and setter
points: Attributes are the name/value pairs inside an opening tag: src on an img, href on an a, class on almost anything.
One argument reads: $("img").attr("src") returns the attribute value, e.g. the file name drum.png. Useful for diagnosing a broken image (the logged path shows what the browser tried to load).
Two arguments write: $("a").attr("href", "https://www.yahoo.com") changes every selected anchor's destination. Clicking the link then goes to the new URL.
Same rule as .css(): with a second argument it sets; without one it gets.

concepts.heading: Class is an attribute too
points: $("h1").attr("class") returns the full space-separated class string, e.g. big-title margin-50.
(Extra) For adding or removing individual classes prefer addClass/removeClass; attr("class", ...) would overwrite the whole list.
(Extra) When getting, jQuery returns the value of the first matched element; when setting, it applies to all matches.

code_examples.caption: Get and set href (matches reference repo, which uses Bing)
code_examples.code:
console.log($("a").attr("href"));          // current URL
$("a").attr("href", "https://www.bing.com"); // change it

console.log($("h1").attr("class"));       // e.g. big-title margin-50

pitfalls: attr("class", value) replaces all existing classes; use addClass to append.
A src that points at a missing file fails to load; logging attr("src") is a quick way to see the path being requested.

gaps_and_ideas: Tasks for a combined jQuery lesson: log a link's href, change it, swap an img src between two images, read the class attribute. Demo: a button that swaps the picture by changing src.
